title: Medical coordinator (F/M) - Sudan
body:
For more than 40 years, Médecins du Monde (MdM), a campaigning medical organisation committed to international solidarity, has been caring for the most vulnerable populations here and abroad. It has continued to bear witness to obstacles that exist in accessing healthcare and has secured sustainable improvements in health-for-all policies.

Those working for this independent organisation do not solely dispense care and treatment but condemn violations of human dignity and rights and fight to improve matters for populations living in precarious situations.

MdM France currently works in 30 countries across all continents to facilitate access to healthcare through 6 political battles:

- Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights
- Migration, Exile, Human Rights and Health
- Harm Reduction
- Environment and Health
- Humanitarian Space
- Healthcare systems and rights

**MdM in Sudan**

MdM maintained a presence in Jebel Marra until 2011. Mid-December 2025, MdM decided to launch an exploratory mission in West Darfur and allocated core funds to provide medicines, recruit an exploratory team composed of a head of mission, a medical coordinator and a logistics coordinator, and start activities in Darfur.

Since end of April 2026, MdM is managing a clinic in the Dar Omo camp in Feina (South Darfur) hosting approximately 25.000 displaced persons.

Since August 2026, 2 mobile clinics are operating around Feina and mid-September 2026, MdM has launched a response to a cholera outbreak in North Darfur.

MdM France has decided to register itself and consolidate its presence in East Sudan to have a balanced presence in all Sudan and be able to answer humanitarian needs in this part of the country.

**About the role**

You are in charge of designing, planning, implementing, adapting and monitoring health activities. You directly manage the medical team.

**What you’ll do**

- Participate in the definition of the country strategy led by the general coordinator and drive the medical and technical aspects in the development of this strategy
- Design, plan, implement, adapt and monitor the programme’s health activities
- Ensure the quality and relevance of health activities, supervise the collection and analysis of medical data
- Recruit, manage, train, and motivate the medical team
- Ensure the management of pharmaceutical products
- Carry out health needs assessments and evaluations of medical partners
- Monitor, analyse and share health and epidemiological data and assess needs and contribute to medical response planning and emergency preparedness for epidemics and mass displacement
- Cooperate with the administration team regarding budgeting and supervise the medical purchase process
- Represent MdM with authorities, partners and other NGOs on health issues
- Participate in the writing of proposals and reports

**Who you’ll work with**

You work under the supervision of the general coordinator of the mission (based in El Geneina) and in collaboration with the health advisor, the MHPSS advisor and the pharmacy officer based at HQ. You manage directly the activity manager and the pharmacy officer. In Feina, the medical team is composed of a medical team supervisor and a midwife supervisor.

**You are the right match if you:**

- Have a medical degree (medical doctor, nurse, midwife)
- Have a minimum 4 years of experience in the humanitarian sector in a similar position
- Have experience in emergency responses, outbreak management, nutrition, health assessments and medical programme start-up
- Demonstrate experience working in complex, politically sensitive or rapidly evolving environments
- Are able to work in high security context
- Have solid background in team leadership, capacity building and technical supervision
- Have strong communication, negotiation and diplomacy skills
- Have strong ability to work collaboratively with diverse teams and multicultural stakeholders
- Have excellent organisational and time-management skills
- Have mapping skills with Google Earth or ArcGIS
- Have strong proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
- Are fluent in English (spoken and written); knowledge of Arabic is an asset

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Are not aligned with MdM’s values
- Don't have experience in volatile security environments

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

Contract & status:

- Gross monthly salary: 3 663 €
- Fixed-term contract starting as soon as possible and for 6 months
- Single posting

Work environment:

- Position based in El Geneina , West Darfur, with regular field visits

Benefits:

- 13th month salary (paid in 2 installments after 6 months of service)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

Essentials:

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumondeh.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumondeh.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know

title: Engineering and Shelter Team leader
body:
DRC Uganda is currently looking for a highly qualified and motivated individual to join our dynamic team as an Engineering and Shelter Team Leader.

**The overall purpose of the role:**

The Engineering and Shelter Team Leader will be responsible for providing overall technical leadership and oversight for shelter and infrastructure activities across Bidibidi, Rhino Camp and Imvepi refugee settlements. He/she will oversee cash-for-shelter assistance, renovation and construction works, ensuring quality and compliance with required technical standards. The position holder will also supervise Engineering Assistants and work closely with programme teams, Supply Chain, contractors and relevant stakeholders to ensure timely and effective implementation of shelter activities.

**Please note that this position is contingent upon confirmation of funding.**

**Your main duties and responsibilities will be:**

**Technical leadership and programme implementation**

- Provide overall technical leadership and oversight for shelter, renovation and construction activities across Bidibidi, Rhino Camp and Imvepi.
- Lead planning and implementation of shelter activities and ensure that agreed targets, timelines and technical standards are achieved.
- Review and approve technical assessments, Bill of Quantities (BOQs), cost estimates, specifications and other technical documentation prepared by Engineering Assistants before implementation.
- Provide technical guidance on appropriate shelter repair solutions, materials, designs and construction approaches, ensuring value for money, safety and suitability to the operational context.
- Ensure shelter and infrastructure interventions comply with approved project designs, organizational procedures and applicable humanitarian and technical standards.
- Ensure timely technical verification and documentation of completed household shelter repairs and follow-up of identified quality or safety concerns.
- Work closely with Protection, Cash and MEAL teams to ensure effective referral, assessment, monitoring and accountability throughout the cash-for-shelter assistance cycle.

**Renovation, construction and contractor management**

- Lead technical assessments and development/review of BOQs, drawings, specifications and cost estimates for project-supported renovation and construction works.
- Work closely with Supply Chain during procurement processes, including providing technical input into solicitation documents, technical evaluation of bids and clarification of technical requirements.
- Coordinate and monitor contractors during implementation to ensure compliance with approved BOQs, specifications, work plans, timelines and contractual requirements.
- Review progress and completed works and provide technical verification/certification to support acceptance and payment processes in accordance with organizational procedures.
- Identify construction defects, delays, variations and other technical risks and ensure appropriate corrective measures are agreed upon and followed through.

**Budget and resource management**

- Monitor expenditure against planned shelter activities and provide timely input into budget forecasts, spending plans and Budget Versus Actual (BVA) reviews.
- Track planned procurements, works and cash-for-shelter requirements to identify potential underspending, overspending or implementation delays and recommend corrective actions.
- Ensure BOQs and cost estimates are realistic, technically justified and provide value for money.
- Work closely with Finance, Supply Chain and the Project Manager to ensure timely procurement and utilization of resources required for shelter activities.

**Team management and capacity building**

- Provide day-to-day supervision and technical guidance to Engineering Assistants, including allocation of tasks, review of deliverables and monitoring of performance.
- Conduct regular field monitoring and provide coaching, mentoring and technical support to team members.
- Identify capacity-building needs and facilitate technical orientation and on-the-job training for shelter staff and other relevant project personnel.
- Promote effective teamwork, accountability and communication within the shelter team and with other programme and support departments.

**Coordination and stakeholder engagement**

- Represent the project on shelter and infrastructure matters in relevant coordination meetings, technical working groups and engagements as delegated by the Project Manager.
- Maintain effective working relationships with the Office of the Prime Minister (OPM), United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), district/local government authorities, settlement leadership, communities, implementing partners and other relevant stakeholders.
- Coordinate closely with community structures and assisted households to promote participation, accountability and ownership throughout implementation.
- Liaise with contractors, suppliers and relevant technical stakeholders to address implementation challenges and ensure timely delivery of works.
- Ensure effective internal coordination with Protection, Cash, MEAL, Finance and Supply Chain teams.

**About you**

To be successful in this role, you must have a minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience in civil/building engineering, shelter, construction or infrastructure programming, preferably within humanitarian or development contexts. Moreover, we also expect the following.

**Required**

- Bachelor's degree in civil engineering, Building Engineering, Construction Management or another relevant engineering field.
- Experience in using design software like AutoCAD, ArchiCAD, Revit, QGIS software etc.
- Demonstrated experience in supervising construction, renovation and/or shelter programmes, including preparation and review of BOQs, drawings, specifications and cost estimates.
- Strong understanding of construction quality assurance, site supervision, occupational safety, and relevant engineering standards
- Experience working with refugees and host communities.
- Ability to ride a motorcycle with valid class “A” permit

**Desirable**

- A relevant postgraduate degree in Civil Engineering, Building Engineering, Construction Management or another relevant engineering field.
- Knowledge of one or more languages commonly spoken in the operational areas.
- Experience with cash-based shelter programming or household-level shelter repair assistance

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

- Contract length: 10 months
- Band: MG 2
- Designation of Duty Station: Bidibidi
- Start date: November 2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national employees; please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-drc/vacancies).

title: Project Director (f/m/d) (100%)
body:
***Time Commitment***: The initial contract duration is until July 2027, with the possibility of an extension depending on project funding. A long-term commitment is preferred.

***Location***: Ioannina, Greece

**About the Organization and the Project**

Be Aware And Share (BAAS) is an independent non-profit organization that supports people affected by forced displacement and oppressed communities and stands against fortress Europe. Founded in 2015 in Switzerland, BAAS is primarily engaging in working with and for people on the move in Europe. Currently, the organization mainly focuses on its Community Center in Ioannina, Greece where a variety of services are offered. BAAS also carries out awareness-raising activities in Switzerland. All BAAS work is financed exclusively by donations.

**Job Description**

We are seeking a dedicated Project Director who will ensure the smooth and efficient running of our operations in Greece. In this dynamic role, you'll oversee project implementation, manage human and financial resources, take the lead for strategic steering, handle logistics, establish and maintain a comprehensive risk management system and support the project team in delivering high-quality services to people on the move. Your leadership will help BAAS navigate the complexities of solidarity work and drive our vision forward. You will be the key link between the operations in Greece and the organization in Switzerland, responsible for driving the Greek legal entity of BAAS and acting as its representative internally and externally. The Project Director reports to the Executive Board of Be Aware And Share.

**Main Responsibilities**

● Guide the strategic development of the project in alignment with the organization’s goals

● Handle all tasks related to the Greek legal entity and act as its representative

● Manage and support the project team, promoting a positive work environment

● Ensure sustainable human resource management, incl. recruitment processes

● Establish and maintain effective monitoring and evaluation systems as per donor requirements

● Conduct regular risk assessments, implement mitigation strategies, and ensure the safety of operations for staff, participants, and the organization

● Ensure adherence to organizational policies and carry out regular policy reviews

● Assist in the preparation and management of the project budget, ensuring financial accountability and sustainability

● Act as Safeguarding Focal Point for incident management and compliance

● Build and maintain relationships with local and regional partners, stakeholders, and communities to enhance project effectiveness and outreach

● Manage all logistical aspects, including apartments, transportation and related resources

**Requirements**

● Minimum 3 years of experience in operations management, preferably within the humanitarian or NGO sector

● Proven track record of managing projects effectively ● Strong understanding of logistics, budgeting, and compliance in non-profit operations

● Familiarity with data management and reporting systems

● Excellent leadership and team management abilities

● Ideally knowledge of Greek legal entities or experience with legal entities in other contexts

● Knowledge of project cycle management, including project identification, planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation

● Strong administrative and organisational skills, with the ability to work and manage autonomously, while also leading a team

● Ability and willingness to work in a dynamic and highly challenging environment

● Ability to work sensitively and effectively in diverse cultural contexts

● Strong organizational skills and attention to detail

● Demonstrated experience in building and maintaining networks with local and international partners

● Flexibility, especially with regard to areas of responsibility and contextual changes

● Excellent written, spoken, and editing skills in English are essential. Strong proficiency in Greek is highly desirable and considered a significant advantage. Arabic, Farsi are assets.

● Category B driver's license, manual transmission and willingness to drive in Greece

**Compensation and Benefits**

● EUR 1,300 net per month

● 21 days of annual leave (excl. public holidays)

● Wide scope for independent work structure and participation in organizational development

● Access to diverse networks and partnerships

● Comprehensive training and introduction to the project and the organization

● The opportunity to take on a responsible position in a committed and dynamic team and to make a crucial contribution to the realization of the BAAS operations in Greece

title: Request for proposals – External Auditor Netherlands
body:
## **About ACAPS**

[ACAPS](http://www.acaps.org/) believes that evidence must be at the heart of humanitarian action and together with our partners we turn data into decisions that truly matter. We cut through the noise and make sense out of chaos. We analyse complex data and provide clear insights so that decision-makers can take the best possible course of action.

We do this by:

- Providing independent analysis that helps humanitarians make informed choices.
- Deploying experts to support assessments and analysis in crisis.
- Driving innovation to collect better, faster, and more reliable data.

Until the end of 2025, ACAPS was a project hosted by the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC). Since 1 January 2026, ACAPS operates as an independent foundation (stichting) registered in the Netherlands.

## **Requested services**

We are looking for a Dutch audit firm to audit the annual financial statements of Stichting ACAPS for financial year 2026 and issue a signed controleverklaring.

FY2026 is our first audited year as an independent organisation. FY2025 was covered by a compilation engagement (samenstelverklaring). ACAPS is expected to qualify as a small legal entity, so this is a voluntary audit, but it must meet the same professional standards as a statutory audit. Annual expenditure is approximately €6.5 million.

The successful audit firm will deliver the following services:

*Audit of the financial statements*

- Audit the FY2026 annual financial statements in accordance with Dutch auditing standards (NV COS).
- Issue a signed controleverklaring on whether the financial statements give a true and fair view under Title 9 Book 2 of the Dutch Civil Code and RJ 640 (not-for-profit organisations).
- Check that the Management Board report (bestuursverslag) is consistent with the financial statements.
- Include the sections on fraud and going concern required by the NBA.

*Reporting*

- Provide a management letter (accountantsverslag) with audit findings, internal control observations and prioritised recommendations.
- Present the audit findings to the Board or its audit committee, in English.
- Follow up on previous recommendations in later years of the contract.
    
    *Donor-specific reports (optional)*

Some donors and lead partners require separate assurance reports, such as NV COS 800/805 reports or agreed-upon procedures. These are not part of the core audit. Please quote them separately, per report. We will confirm the final list at contract signature.

**Areas of specific attention**

As this is a first-year audit following our separation from NRC, we expect the following areas to need specific attention:

- Opening balances on 1 January 2026, transferred from NRC. ACAPS holds the supporting documentation and has read-only access to the relevant NRC records.
- Income recognition across three funding routes: grants signed directly with donors, sub-agreements under grants held by NRC, and partnerships led by other NGOs, including EU-funded actions.
- Restricted funds, deferred income and balances with NRC and other lead partners.
- Personnel costs, our largest expense, across three employment models: direct employment in the Netherlands, staff hosted by a partner organisation, and employer-of-record providers.
- Allocation of staff time and other costs to grants.
- Related-party transactions, in particular with NRC.
- Presentation of the FY2025 comparative figures, which are unaudited and not comparable to FY2026.
- Introduction of a new ERP system during 2026.

## Indicative timeline

**Milestone and Indicative date**

- Contract award and engagement letter: November – December 2026
- Planning meeting and information request list (min. 4 weeks before start of interim audit): December 2026
- Interim audit: internal control and opening balances: January – February 2027
- ACAPS delivers year-end file and draft financial statements: 31 March 2027
- Year-end fieldwork: April 2027
- Draft auditor’s report and management letter:15 May 2027
- Presentation to the Supervisory Council and Management Board: Latest 30 May 2027
- Signed controleverklaring and final management letter: 5 June 2027

## Requirements

- Dutch audit firm registered with the NBA and authorised to issue a controleverklaring.
- An engagement partner who is a Registeraccountant (RA) or Accountant-Administratieconsulent (AA) with certifying authority.
- A licence from the AFM under the Wta is preferred. Firms without one should show a satisfactory recent quality review.
- Experience auditing non-profit organisations funded by institutional and government donors, under RJ 640.
- Experience with first-year audits, ideally of organisations that separated from a host agency.
- Experience with organisations that have an international workforce.
- An engagement partner and manager who can work and report in English.
- Independence from ACAPS, its Supervisory Council and its management.

title: SOUTH SUDAN - GRANTS MANAGER (M/F) - JUBA
body:
## About us

**Desired start date:** 08/02/2027  
**Duration of the mission: 6** months  
**Location:** Juba - South Sudan

  
**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in some twenty countries, the SI teams – 2500 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL (SI) has been operating in South Sudan since 2006, conducting activities in emergency and post emergency context.

\- Food insecurity is one of the highest in the world due to recurring shocks (consecutive years of widespread flooding, conflict-based displacement), and an ongoing protracted macro-economic crisis.  
\- The country also faces cholera outbreaks on a yearly basis, has very limited sanitation coverage and safe water access remain a challenge for most of the population.  
\- On top of these chronic situations, South Sudan has been highly impacted by the war that started in Sudan in April 2023. As of mid 2026, more than 1,300,000 people have entered South Sudan, the vast majority entering through the Joda/ Wunthow border point in Renk County, Upper Nile State (northern part of South Sudan).  
\- In 2025 internal tensions increased at government level and have led to wide spread conflicts within the country. Elections at the end of 2026 may not happen as planned.  
\- An Ebola outbreak is currently at its doors in DRC and Uganda.  
As a result, 10 million are in need of humanitarian assistance as of 2026.

  
**SI sectors of intervention:**  
\- The portfolio includes both WASH & FSL activities. SI's expertise in running emergency WaSH intervention is highly acknowledged by all WaSH actors and donors. SI has also been one of the first responders of the cholera response. Recent fundings have allowed increasing significantly the FSL component on the mission  
**Areas of operation:**  
**SI is present:**  
\- In Upper Nile, SI has an office in Renk and a sub-office in Malakal. The response has focused on cholera and drought while maintaining life saving WASH services for returnees and refugees in the two main transit centres of the country.  
\- SI has opened a base in Ulang in 2025 (State of Upper Nile but under another base/Field Coordinator)  
\- In addition, SI has a rapid emergency team (ERRM) based in Juba, who is being deployed following Rapid Needs Assessment in flood, epidemic or conflict induced displacement in the country.  
**Size of operations:**  
In 2026, the mission’s estimated budget is around USD 10 million, and 140 employees following an ongoing scale up on the last quarter of 2025.  
The mission is currently funded by ECHO (3 grants), DoS, CDCS, FIFSAN, SSHF, Norway MoFA, FCDO.

## About the job

**General objective:**

Under the supervision and with the support of the Grants and Partnership Coordinator, the Grant Manager role on general Grant Manager tasks and on supporting project development and diversification of funding sources.

Specifically, he/she is in charge of:

• Contributing to the mission’s strategic development.

• Monitoring and identifying funding opportunities in line with SI country and global strategy.

• Overseeing compilation of timely and high-quality proposals, reports and contract modification requests for submission to donors and consortium partners.

• Monitoring compliance with donor procedures throughout the grant cycle and building capacity of new and existing staff on internal accountability tools and donor procedures.

• Proactively following-up on donor contractual obligations, from contracting to closing and archiving, and ensuring contractual obligations are known and understood by relevant staff/departments.

• Developing partnerships with national partners and reinforcing SI localization strategy (tools, partner identification)

• Managing the partnership with other partners of consortiums

**The main challenges:**

• Contributing to the mission’s strategic development.

• Diversifying fundings sources in line with SI country and global strategy.

• Increasing the quality of reporting and proposal development.

**Priorities of the 2-3 first months:**

• Finalize the back and forth with the donors on the proposals, especially the ECHO HIP proposals

• Follow-up on donor contractual obligations on the current and future donor contract

• Management and capacity building of the Reporting and Communication Officer under the direct management

## Your profile

**Education / academic background:**

- Master Degree in humanitarian/development studies, social sciences, management or other related discipline.
- 3-4 years in the humanitarian sector
- 1-2 years on a similar position

**Specific skills and experience:**

- Experience in developing proposals for institutional donors.
- Experience in capacity building of staff.
- Experience in developing concept notes and strategy papers.
- Excellent writing skills & Excel usage.
- Experience in managing audits and compliance risks.
- Experience in budget follow-up.
- Experience in developing localization strategies.
- Good organization skills. Rigorous & detail-oriented profile
- Good coordination and diplomacy.
- Good stress management.
- Experience working with SI (or a similar organization) is an asset.
- Prior experience in South Sudan would be considered as an asset.

**Language:**

- Fluent in English, written and spoken.
- Arabic is an asset.

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**

**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2150 gross per month (2150 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 700.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

- The Grants Manager is living in a shared guesthouse with the other international staffs.
- Individual room, with electricity 24/7.
- Internet and Phone network available
- Restaurants and international food are available

There is an internal curfew at night for international staffs - different zones are set (6-8-10PM). Curfew can be reduced based on security updates  
There is one driver available on evenings for movements out of office hours, 2 drivers during weekends daytime.  
Access to activities is possible for all (and encouraged!).  
In coordination, movements outside of Juba town (besides intervention location) for leisure are not permitted.

title: NIGERIA - GRANTS & PARTNERSHIP HEAD OF DEPARTMENT (M/F) - ABUDJA
body:
## About us

**Desired start date: 15/12/2026**  
**Duration of the mission: 12 months**  
**Location: ABUJA**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

**Solidarites International** launched its operation in Nigeria in 2016 as a consequence of the humanitarian needs of displaced populations and host communities caused by the current crisis with conflict and the ongoing violence in the North-East of Nigeria led by Armed Opposition Groups since 2009. The security situation and epidemics/outbreaks continue to affect millions of lives in Northeastern and North Western parts of Nigeria. As of June 2022, according to IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix, an estimated 2.2 million people are displaced within Borno State which remains, for a major part, inaccessible to humanitarian actors.

The targeted sectors of intervention are WASH, Shelter, RRM, Food Security & Livelihoods. The annual budget of the mission is around 8.3 million euros in 2022.

The mission is organized with a coordination office in Maiduguri and 3 bases located in Ngala, Dikwa and Monguno managed remotely from Maiduguri for the North-East. In the North-West, Solidarites International is conducting activities on 3 bases located in Gusau, Anka and Taleta in Zamfara State. Abuja is the representative for the mission Nigeria.

Mission staff : 165  
The Grants and Partnership HOD will directly manage the Grants coordination team composed of :   
\- A Reporting & Communications Officer   
She/he will closely work with all Departmental Heads, Field Coordinators and Project Managers of the mission.   
The Grants and Partnership HOD will report to the Country Director and be in link with Grants & Partnership department in HQ.

## About the job

**General objective:**

Working closely with the programmes and support departments, the Head of Grants and Partnerships Department is responsible for managing relations with donors, as well as developing and monitoring the country office's funding strategy. They supervise, adapt and optimise working methods and tools dedicated to managing donor accountability.   
They validate contractual documents (project proposals, reports, requests for amendments, partnership agreements, etc.) before they are submitted.   
They play a key role in defining the country office's partnership strategy and coordinates relations with the various implementing partners (see the partnership implementation framework). Ensures effective coordination between departments for grant management and provides strategic support to the country office in relation to donor relations, external representation, management of implementing partners, external compliance and accountability to donors.

**The main challenges:**

\- Access challenges and remote management due to security contraints in some areas of intervention  
\- Strategic positionning in a global trend of funding decrease   
\- Focus on partnership and localization in all areas of intervention. This requires adapted operational modalities and a support to local partners.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

\*Support the programmatic strategy (2027-2032) and PROG 2027 implementation  
\*Monitoring of partnerships and capacity building plan in coordination with other Department (Programs, E & C, etc.)  
\*Follow up on the advancement of the financing contracts   
\*Finalize partnership management/localization strategy  
\*Coordinate proposals   
\*Continue developing relationship with donor representatives and engage internally/ externally with different interlocutors to identify new funding opportunities

**Security constraints:**

No walking policy everywhere in the country / Security situation calm in Abuja, level 2 (out of 5), Maiduguri is level 3 and level 4 in other bases/sub-bases.

## Your profile

**Diploma and Experience :**

Diploma : Bachelor or masters in a related degree: humanitarian response, international cooperation

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 5 years and more

Experience on similar positions : 3/4 years

**SKILLS :**

**Technical skills**

1. Excellent reporting, writing and proof reading skills
2. Strong knowledge of main donors (ECHO, French donors, SIDA etc) and their respective policies / guidelines
3. Previous experience and achievements in developing strategic partnerships with other NGOs (MoUs, negotiations, governance, capacity building ...)
4. Proven ability to deal with donors and operational partners

**Transversal skills**

1. Critical thinking skills and the ability to adapt to fast-paced environments, while working independently to meet tight deadlines with minimal supervision
2. Good knowledge of the humanitarian project cycle management;
3. Excellent communication, networking skills, organizational and prioritization skills, ability to multi-task, Capacity to adapt and show organizational flexibilit
4. External representation

**Languages :**

1. English (fluent - Mandatory)
2. French (an asset)

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The Grant & Partnership HOD will be based in Abuja with frequent field visit expected in the regional offices (Maiduguri. Birnin Kebbi and potentially Gusau or Sokoto).   
In Abuja, living condition are good and all commodities and goods (local or imported) can be found (supermarket, restautant, cinema, sport centers ...). Abuja GH is Comfortable with private bedroom and bathroom, 24/7 electricity and internet. GH is located in the same estate as the office, avoiding taking the car every morning but still clearly separated from working area (not the same building). Estate where GH/Office is located is providing Gym room, Swimming pool and squash court.  
At base level, (Maiduguri, Birnin Kebbi and Gusau), the bases offers a comfortable environment, in spite of limited movements outside of the compound for security reasons. The Guest House offers good living conditions, with private bedroom and bathroom and shared & comfortable common spaces. Electricity and internet are available at the office and at the GH at all times. Ping pong, pool table and some gym equipment are available in the GH in Maiduguri. All essential good (food, hygiene etc..) can be bought locally in the small shops around the office, or in the pre-validated supermarket. Visits to other NGOs are possible, as well as some pre-validated places (hotel and restaurants).  
Occasional field visit in NE sub bases, to ensure a correct program overview depedning on the security context and validation. No Overnight are possible in NE sub bases, only daily round trip with UNHAS are possible.

title: Emergency Response Manager Sudan
body:
**Background:**

The Emergency Response Manager (ERM) will oversee the overall country emergency response programme.

The ERM will lead on the coordination, quality response, management, and reporting of emergency response activities including those under the ECHO-funded Emergency Response consortium (FaSER) and UN pipelines. The ERM will support and provide technical supervision of emergency response teams in the field to respond to rapid onset crises related to conflict displacement and natural disasters, coordinating all emergency preparedness plans, minimum prepared actions (MPAs), and supervise emergency activities across NRC’s geographical spread in Sudan.

This will include pre-planning, assessment, coordination, leadership and overseeing emergency responses, in collaboration with Area Managers, Programme Specialists and other relevant programme and support departments, including safety and security and cash and market-based programming.

The role will also play a crucial function as surge capacity and will be deployed to hotspot locations across Sudan to reinforce critical emergency response programming depending on the needs of the operation.

**What you will do:**

Generic responsibilities:

1. Ensure adherence to NRC policies, handbooks, procedures and SOPs/guidelines;
2. Overall oversight, strategic development, and operational management of emergency response interventions across the Country Office;
3. Development of robust emergency set-ups based on appropriate needs analysis with an integrated programme approach;
4. Development of emergency response strategies and technical SOPs/guidelines;
5. Development and management of funding proposals, project budgets and donor reports;

Specific responsibilities:

1. **ERM Consortium Programme Management:**

- Overall responsibility for effective and efficient coordination of the emergency preparedness and response projects consistent with the project management cycle *(including reporting to the desired quality and standard)*;
- Overall budget management for FaSER projects/portfolio implemented and ensure appropriate burn-rates are maintained and that solutions to over/under expenditure are applied;
- Develop strategies, set-ups, and continuous review of technical guidance, tools, and SOPs for the overall emergency response

**2. Emergency Surge Support**

- Provide general programme support to key Area Offices during emergency responses including directly overseeing cash and other distributions.
- Lead and develop Emergency Response plans to coordinate NRC’s overall response to an emergency and provide inputs for use in fund raising, advocacy and programme development
- Lead coordination meetings with Programme, Support and Area Office colleagues.

**3. Coordination and Representation:**

- Liaise and coordinate with UN and I/NGO partners, local authorities, and beneficiaries in planning and response to emergencies, preparedness, and contextual understanding of areas of operations;
- Represent the RRM Consortium to external stakeholders - donors, government, coordination bodies, and local and international NGOs. Include the Steering Committee and other consortium staff in representation as much as possible and as appropriate. Network with relevant actors to help achieve consortium objectives;
- Conduct senior representation at state level and promote strong working relationships with government counterparts;

Please refer to the detailed [Job Description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQBuZJQ-ramxQq178rbecg-aATvc50YqX3Sjy3I3YrYyE9A?e=NEqRjT) as the above enlisted responsibilities are just a snapshot.

**What you will bring:**

1. **Generic professional competencies:**

- At least five years in a humanitarian programming environment, including three years’ experience in project management position;
- Previous working experience in implementing emergency programme cycle in complex, fragile, and volatile contexts;
- Must have experience in cash-based programming, specifically cash distribution modalities;
- Emergency Response expertise, including Rapid Response Mechanisms (RRM) or Emergency Response Mechanisms (ERM);
- Technical expertise in one of NRC’s Core Competencies (Shelter/NFI, WASH, ICLA, Education, Camp Management/Protection from Violence), is added advantage;
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities;
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal;
- Computer literacy in Microsoft Office, including strong skills in Excel.

1. **Context/ Specific skills, knowledge and experience:**

- Keen interest and knowledge of the context in Sudan, previous experience in Sudan is very valuable;
- Arabic language skills is an advantage;
- Previous experience working with/ in consortiums and multi-agency projects;
- Specific experience in camp-contexts, distributions, cash programming and shelter/NFI
- Strong skills in analysis and coordination
- Experience in needs assessment, project monitoring and evaluation, and programme development;
- Strong leadership skills and a supportive management style;
- Experience of a flexible approach to managing and prioritising a high and diverse workload;
- Proven ability to work effectively across cultures, in sensitive environments and with stakeholders at all levels.

- **What we offer:**
- Duty station: Al-Geniena, Darfur, Sudan
- Contract: 12 Months (renewable based on funding and performance)
- Travel: 80%
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s either **national or international** salary scale.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- *For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity MarketPlace.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Applicants who do not fill in the required information will not be considered for the role.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Mandatory to submit the below when applying:
    - **Your most updated English CV and remove all previous outdated CVs.**
    - **Your most updated Cover Letter**
    - **Do not attach certificates or any other documents apart from the two mentioned above.**
    - **Incomplete applications will not be considered.**
- **This position is open for both national and international candidates. Internals might be assessed first if the pool is competitive.**
- We receive many applications for each vacant position. Therefore, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **esa.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.
- [Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)
- [Learn more about Sudan](https://www.nrc.no/countries/africa/sudan/)

title: Development of a vector control training package for wash and health practitioners in the africa region.
body:
(Find the complete folder with all relevant information including the [RFP here](https://rodekruis.sharepoint.com/sites/Meetingsinternational/Gedeelde%20%20documenten/Public%20documents/IH%20Procurement%20public%20documents/RFP%20-%20Log-2026-1374%20Vector%20Control%20Training?d=w2f16674c6c2f4567b3946c075513f3fd&csf=1&web=1&e=0j4Puk))

**Terms of Reference**

**Title of Assignment**

Development of a Vector Control Training Package for WASH and Health Practitioners in the Africa Region

**Project Name**

WASH Surge Localization Programme

**Project Country**

Global (pilot training to be conducted in Ethiopia or South Sudan)

**1. Introduction**

The Netherlands Red Cross (NLRC) and partners are working to strengthen local capacities for emergency preparedness, anticipatory action, and response across Africa. In line with their auxiliary role to the public authorities, and within the framework of localization, National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies frequently act as first responders during disease outbreaks, flooding, displacement crises, and other emergencies.

Vector-borne diseases continue to pose a significant public health burden in many countries where the Red Cross and Red Crescent National Societies operate. At the same time, vector control knowledge among WASH and Health practitioners varies considerably. There is a need for accessible, practical training materials that can be used by National Societies, surge personnel, and humanitarian practitioners to improve knowledge and decision-making related to vector control.

The NLRC therefore seeks a consultant to develop a comprehensive training package on vector control that can be delivered by facilitators with a fair understanding of the subject matter. The package will be piloted during a training event planned for December 2026 in either Ethiopia or South Sudan.

**2. Background and Context**

Vector-borne diseases remain among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in many humanitarian settings. Climate change, population movements, urbanization, environmental degradation, and weak health systems are contributing to changes in disease transmission patterns and increasing the risk of outbreaks.

Humanitarian organizations are increasingly expected to integrate vector control considerations into emergency preparedness, response, recovery, and resilience programmes. While specialist expertise is sometimes available, many WASH and Health practitioners involved in programme design and implementation have limited formal training in vector control.

The Red Cross movement has an important role to play through:

- Community engagement , risk communication and behaviour change
- Environmental management
- Vector surveillance and risk assessment
- Support to outbreak preparedness and response including community-based surveillance
- Coordination with health and WASH actors
- Integration of vector control into humanitarian programming

To strengthen these capacities, a practical training package is required that can be delivered in different country contexts and adapted to local disease priorities.

**3. Purpose, Objectives and Deliverables**

**Purpose**

To develop a practical, participatory and easy-to-facilitate vector control training package for WASH and Health practitioners working in humanitarian and development settings.

**Overall Objective**

To increase the knowledge and understanding of vector-borne disease prevention and vector control among WASH and Health practitioners, enabling them to support the design, implementation and monitoring of appropriate vector control interventions.

**Specific Objectives**

The training package should enable participants to:

- Understand the epidemiology and transmission pathways of major vector-borne diseases.
- Understand the roles and responsibilities of WASH, Health and community actors in vector control.
- Conduct basic vector-related risk assessments.
- Select appropriate vector control interventions based on context and risk.
- Understand operational, environmental and safety considerations.
- Integrate vector control into preparedness, anticipatory action and humanitarian emergency responses.
- Coordinate with relevant health, WASH and government stakeholders.

**Scope of the Training Package**

The consultant should develop a 3 days training package with different modules and exercises, allowing for a one to three days training depending on the modules used.

The training should cover, at minimum:

**Vector-borne Diseases**

Introduction to: Malaria (with description of different malaria carrying subspecies) Dengue, Chikungunya, Yellow Fever, Schistosomiasis, Trypanosomiasis and other relevant diseases common in African humanitarian settings

**Vector Control Approaches**

Introduction to Environmental mechanical biological and chemical and integrated Vector Management (IVM).

**Humanitarian Context**

The context considered for the training include, vector control during emergencies**,** vector control during displacement and camp settings, Flood-related vector risks, Urban vector control challenges as well as for the Red Cross important Community-based approaches, and Protection, Gender and Inclusion (PGI)

**Planning and Decision Making**

The training should include a section focusing on health and surveillance data, risk assessment, Intervention selection, Monitoring and evaluation, Coordination mechanisms

**Safety and Environmental Considerations**

This should include Safe handling of equipment and chemicals Environmental risks Waste management Safeguarding and community acceptance

**Emerging and other relevant Topics**

Climate change and vector-borne diseases Insecticide resistance, new and emerging vector control tools such as spatial repellents, Operational challenges in humanitarian settings

**Deliverables**

- The consultant will with the support of the NLRC and UNICEF will be expected to provide: Review and compilation of existing vector control training materials from organizations such as: IFRC, WHO, UNICEF and NGO’s working on vector control and identify materials that can be adapted and referenced.
- The consultant will develop a complete facilitator package in English including: Facilitator guide, Agenda for a 3-day version, Session plans, Facilitation notes, Interactive exercises Possible case studies and group work exercises, Quizzes and knowledge checks
- Participant package that should include: Participant manual, Handouts, Reference materials, Reading list Links to online resources
- PowerPoint presentation deck(s) suitable for use by non-specialist facilitators.
- Training evaluation package including: Pre-training assessment Post-training assessment Participant evaluation forms
- Facilitation of a pilot training in December 2026 in Ethiopia South Sudan or other country in the region and incorporation of lessons learned into the final training package(optional).

**4. Profile of the Desired Consultant**

The consultant should possess:

- Minimum 7 years of professional experience in vector control, public health, entomology, or related fields.
- Demonstrated experience in humanitarian settings.
- Experience with vector control in Africa, preferably in both emergency and development contexts.
- Proven experience in developing training curricula and adult learning materials.
- Strong facilitation skills.
- Experience working with Red Cross/Red Crescent, UN agencies, government institutions or international NGOs is an advantage.
- Excellent written and spoken English.
- Experience integrating participatory adult learning methodologies.

**5. Methodology**

The consultant is expected to:

1. Conduct a brief desk review of existing training resources.
2. Consult with NLRC, IFRC, UNICEF and selected technical experts.
3. Develop draft training materials.
4. Revise materials based on feedback.
5. Facilitate the pilot training.
6. Produce a final training package reflecting lessons learned from the pilot.

**6. Planning**

Indicative timeline:

**Activity Timeline**

Contracting consultant - Week of 9th November 2026

Desk review and consultations - November 20th 2026

Draft training package - November 25th 2026

Review and revisions - December 5th 2026

Pilot training (optional time permitting) - December 2026

Final training package - December 2026

**7. Climate and Environmental Impact**

The consultant should ensure that:

- The training promotes environmentally responsible vector control approaches.
- Environmental and ecological risks of vector control interventions are adequately addressed.
- Preference is given to sustainable and integrated vector management approaches.
- Training delivery methods minimize environmental impact where feasible.

**8. Responsibilities and Communication**

The assignment will be coordinated by:

- Jan Heeger, WASH Programme Advisor, NLRC
- Selam Seje, Health Advisor, NLRC
- Joey de Hamer, Programme Manager, NLRC
- Peter Mamburi IFRC technical focal points

**Submission Deadline**

The proposal shall be submitted before the deadline for reception of applications on the 4th of October 2026.

Submission Method

- Proposals must be submitted electronically by email at logistics@redcross.nl with a cc. to JdeHamer@redcross.nl.

The assignment, including the submission of the final invoice, must be completed no later than 31 December 2026.

**Bid Format**

- Email subject must be: Log-2026-1374 – Development of a Vector Control Training Package + \[Name of the bidder\]
- The attachments to be included are described in the next section.
- Language: All documents shall be submitted in English.

**9. Required Documents**

1. **Cover Letter**
2. **Curricula Vitae**
3. **Technical Proposal and methodology**
4. **Financial Proposal** (budget with clear breakdown of fee and overheads if applicable);
5. **Previous Samples:** Applicants must provide at least one, and up to two, samples of previous written work similar to that described in the ToR (such as prior health related training provided), with any sensitive information redacted.
6. **Vendor Registration Form**: Bidders are required to complete the \[[*Annex 2: NLRC Vendor Registration Form*](https://rodekruis.sharepoint.com/sites/Meetingsinternational/_layouts/15/guestaccess.aspx?share=ETvU5WP-Qq5Ah7aIFhh7RXYBKEjBFDi3JiyiO3IV3PlULQ&e=3Nh0Er)\] and submit all relevant supporting documentation referenced in the form (Administrative checklist, Part 1 and 1.9 Environmental standards).

**Vendor Code of Conduct**

NLRC is committed to upholding the highest sustainability standards and requirements (ethical, social, environmental and quality) in all our business providing high-quality services and products. Complying with all laws and regulations and ensuring fair competition are fundamental to this commitment.

The \[[*NLRC Vendor Code of Conduct - Annex 3*](https://rodekruis.sharepoint.com/sites/Meetingsinternational/_layouts/15/guestaccess.aspx?share=IQDkY_CmSWcBQ4W9oHAtgqC8ARRb9CRv9LFAU3eQCgyeOVM&e=FCc7JJ)\], expresses the expectations we hold for all NLRC vendors. The Vendor Code of Conduct outlines the behaviours expected of Vendors who commit to uphold these standards and prevent misconduct. It is legally binding and forms an integral part of the contract between the Vendor and the NLRC. The winning applicants will be requested to sign this Code of Conduct at contract stage.

**Climate & Environmental Impact**

The NLRC has signed an environmental charter. As we work towards ensuring that all our operations coincide with this new agreement, we must also demand that any collaborations we have with external parties also falls within the parameters of this charter.

Please complete the section 1.9 Environmental standards in the Vendor Registration Form \[[*NLRC\_Vendor Registration Form.docx*](https://rodekruis.sharepoint.com/sites/Meetingsinternational/_layouts/15/guestaccess.aspx?share=IQBTNSN4OdU7QISbXbwiWsG6AZBy_YDVy667BGqqVVp3tCg&e=8aZ3gj)\] and provide any additional documents that could illustrate your environmental engagement.

The consultant will work closely with NLRC and IFRC technical staff throughout the assignment and present draft outputs for review and approval.

title: Oficial de Cadena de Suministro - Maracaibo
body:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Cadena de Suministro** altamente calificado con sede en **Maracaibo, Edo. Zulia.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**Descripción del propósito / objetivo del cargo:**

El Oficial de Cadena de Suministro es responsable de todas las adquisiciones de bienes y servicios, almacenamiento, transporte de bienes y personas, gestión de flotas de vehículos y apoyo logístico general al programa general en Zulia de conformidad con el marco interno de Danish Refugee Council – DRC y las regulaciones impuestas por los donantes.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Compras**

- Asegurar el cumplimiento de los procesos de compra requeridos para el adecuado funcionamiento de las operaciones de DRC en Maracaibo.
- Colaboración directa con los equipos de programa para la planificación local de las necesidades de compra y logísticas de los programas de DRC en Zulia.
- Generar seguimiento y trazabilidad de las solicitudes de compra.
- Validar la integridad documental de los procesos según los requerimientos de los donantes.
- Contacto con proveedores para cotizaciones y evaluaciones de compras locales.
- Comunicación directa con proveedores relacionados con la entrega de insumos en los programas de DRC.
- Seguimiento a devoluciones o reclamaciones con proveedores.
- Preparación de solicitudes de pago para el trámite de los equipos de Finanzas de DRC.
- Cualquier otra tarea que le asigne el Gerente de Línea / Técnico.

**Logística**

- Asegurar la entrega oportuna de los materiales solicitados, teniendo en cuenta los procesos y tiempos establecidos por DRC.
- Control, registro y seguimiento de los activos fijos gestionados en la oficina local.
- Realizar inventarios y llevar el control detallado del inventario general de DRC.
- Garantizar la gestión de los servicios generales para los equipos de trabajo (alojamiento, personal, visitantes, oficinas, lugares de almacenamiento y seguridad).
- Implementar procesos de registro, control, seguimiento y verificación de elementos del programa asignados al personal y a los logísticos de la oficina.
- En colaboración con el Líder de equipo de Cadena de Suministro apoyar en la inducción al personal de la oficina sobre los procesos de DRC.
- Cualquier otra tarea que le asigne el Gerente de Línea / Técnico.

**Gestión de Almacén**

- Comprobar que todos los activos antiguos y nuevos estén correctamente registrados y etiquetados.
- Gestionar el inventario de suministros de oficina y consumibles.
- Monitorear y administrar las existencias según los procedimientos de almacenamiento de DRC.
- Preparar y revisar todos los informes mensuales de movimiento de inventario antes de enviarlos al Oficial de Cadena de Suministro para su validación.
- Recogida o entrega de mercancías.
- Asegurar que todos los artículos en el almacén estén correctamente almacenados, apilados y contabilizados con precisión en todo momento.

**Gestión de Flota**

- Asegurar el cumplimiento de los procesos de gestión de flota de DRC en Maracaibo, Venezuela.
- Garantizar la disponibilidad de los vehículos para las operaciones de programa.
- Controlar el uso y consumo del servicio de transporte en la oficina local.

**Administración**

- Participar y ayudar en la implementación del ERP (DRC Dynamics).
- Colaboración con la unidad de finanzas para el correcto registro de la cadena de abastecimiento.
- Coordinación con la unidad de finanzas para la oportuna ejecución de los pagos.
- Redacción de contratos y acuerdos marco para la operación local.

**Competencias esenciales:**

- Mínimo 2 años de experiencia en logística humanitaria, adquisiciones, transporte y distribución, almacenamiento y gestión de stocks.
- Vocación de servicio.
- Enfoque al detalle.
- Capacidad de auto-organización.
- Motivación por el trabajo en el sector humanitario.
- Orientación de servicio a los programas.
- Conocimiento de sistemas de ERP para compras.
- Manejo Avanzado de OneDrive, MS Word, Excel y Adobe PDF.
- Capacidades analíticas.
- Orientación a la resolución de problemas.
- Capacidad de trabajo bajo incertidumbre.

*Deseable:*

- Maestría o especialización en Ingeniería de Salud Pública, Ingeniería Hidráulica, Ingeniería Ambiental, Ingeniería Civil, Ingeniería Mecánica, Arquitectura o campo directamente relacionado;
- Carácter tranquilo y diplomático;
- Con conocimientos de aspectos de protección;
- Capacidad para gestionar las prioridades en competencia y cumplir con los plazos;
- Capacidad de crear buen ambiente de equipo y trabajo con socios locales implementadores;
- Manejo del inglés;
- Conocimiento de marco legal venezolano y derecho internacional.

**Educación (Incluir certificados, licencias)**

- Profesional con 2 años de experiencia, Título Universitario pertinente en logística y / o gestión de la cadena de suministro o cualificación profesional equivalente.

**Idiomas:**

- Fluidez en inglés ( Deseable ) escrito y hablado

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda H.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**:

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Domingo 08 de noviembre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado.
