title: Grants and Reporting Officer
body:
**Job Title:** Grants and Reporting Officer

**Function:** Programme Support

**Job Group:** Programmes

**Duty Station:** Odesa, Ukraine (with potential travel to field locations)

**Line Manager:** Programme Development Manager

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/a

**ABOUT US:**

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) reimagines security and civilian protection in areas most impacted by conflict by working alongside communities to interrupt and prevent violence. NP is a global civil society organization that works with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP) and by helping to transform the world’s response to conflict. Programming is founded on unarmed civilian protection and is thematically focused on protection in displacement, child protection, gender-based violence protection and inter-communal violence reduction, social cohesion, and civic engagement.

NP first established a presence in Ukraine in 2014-15 working on peacebuilding and conflict mediation. NP has had a sustained presence in Ukraine since April 2022 and is operational in Kharkiv, Donetska, Dnipropetrovsk, Kherson, Mykolaiv and Odesa oblasts. NP occupies an established space in the protection response in Ukraine; simultaneously providing direct protection to at-risk civilians and providing hands-on support to front-line volunteer collectives to contribute to the sustainability and safety of their actions.

**JOB PURPOSE:**

The Grants and Reporting Officer (GRO) will collaboratively work with the Programmes, Finance and Operational Teams in NP’s Ukraine Country Office to ensure compliance with donor regulations and monitor grant implementation in-line with agreed workplans and objectives. This includes project activity oversight, donor reporting and supporting proposal development (where applicable).

**KEY OBJECTIVES/RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Grants Management and Reporting**

- Lead in drafting narrative donor reports and relevant annexes (i.e. logical frameworks, impact assessments, case studies), ensuring excellent quality, accuracy and adherence to donor guidelines.
- Support programmes, finance and field teams to understand donor contractual requirements, ensuring grant compliance from the outset of grant roll-out (i.e. through inception workshops).
- Maintain information management and involve all internal stakeholders in communications on fundraising issues for grants.
- Lead on updating relevant online platforms (e.g. UN’s Grants Management System (GMS)) with project data and reports, as well as responding to notifications and/or additional information requests from key donors.
- Compile and analyse data to write field activity reports submitted by staff and partners, aligning with grant deliverables.
- Act as team focal point for Salesforce (NP’s global online project management system), including creating new opportunities / projects, updating project activities, monitoring project outputs, tracking progress and extracting relevant information for reporting.
- Coordinate with the finance department to ensure that financial reports are submitted on time, comply with financial reporting requirements and align with narrative reported activity progress.
- Review donor reports, project proposals and communication materials as required.

**Partnership Support**

- Maintain regular communication and coordination with NP’s Partnership department to collect and synthesise data for activity and donor reports.
- Support NP’s Partnership department to draft sub-grant contracts in-line with donor compliance and agreed logframes, objectives and activities.
- Follow up with partners’ implemented activities and report progress through Salesforce.
- Support ad-hoc capacity development requests from partners and provide trainings, guidance and mentoring as needed.

**Other**

- Support with rolling out NPUA’s country strategy across all project sites.
- Travel to project sites to enhance understanding of the context and programming to develop proposals and report to/liaise with donors.
- Undertake other relevant tasks as requested.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND COMPETENCIES:**

**Education, Knowledge, and Experience**

- Excellent and precise command of English, with exemplary oral and written communication skills, and an ability to develop high quality and engaging communications. There is a significant amount of writing required in this position.
- Significant experience developing narrative donor reports (for multilateral and institutional donors including the UN, FCDO, GAC, ECHO, SDC) under minimal supervision.
- Previous grants management, monitoring and evaluation (M&E) or reporting experience within a non-governmental organisation (NGO).
- Experience in institutional donor compliance and familiarity with basic rules and regulations. An understanding of basic statutory requirements would also be an asset.
- Experience in implementing, analysing and utilising M&E tools.
- Experience implementing programmes, ideally in humanitarian emergencies and/or in Ukraine.
- Knowledge or demonstrable interest in civilian protection, human security, violence reduction, protection and/or peacebuilding.
- Relevant university degree in social sciences, international development or related area of studies is preferred but not required. Corresponding work experience will also be considered.

**Skills**

- Diplomacy, professionalism and adept at relationship building.
- Ability to manage sensitive information with discretion.
- Demonstrable conflict analysis skills, identify entry points and design prevention and protection strategies.
- Ability to communicate effectively with individuals and work and live in a multicultural environment.
- Solutions-focused, creative problem solver.
- Genuine commitment to, and interest in, living and working at the community level.
- Flexibility and adaptability.

title: HR and Administration Coordinator
body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified HR and Administration Coordinator.

**About the job**

To provide advice, coordination, capacity building and technical support to HR focal person at field location and overall coordination of HR tasks at country level.

The Human Resources Coordinator ensures compliance to DRC's human resource procedures and guidelines within the country operations. The role contributes to the development of country strategies, which are translated into action plans and day-to-day tasks.

The job is based in Tunis with potential 20% travel to field offices.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

**Human Resources Support**

- Provide technical support and advice to the Human Resources team
- Advise and assist managers in Human Resources related issues and concerns

**Recruitment**

- HR focal person for recruitments of national and expat staff (excluding bands C, D & E with HQ)
- Define and ensure proper onboarding process for new staff
- Coordinate and organize inductions on country level on a regular basis, including coordination with facilitators and participants
- Ensure oversight and consistency in position titles and grades, across all field locations.
- Advise hiring managers in development of Job description, inclusive job advertisements and team structures.

**HR Function and compliance**

- Developing/updating HR policies, Employee/HR Handbook, procedures and tools and close monitoring to ensure compliance.
- Collaborate with Senior Management Team in the analysis of the organizational structure across the three countries to ensure consistency, coherency, and efficiency
- Focal point for DRC coordination office legal matters, liaison with legal Advisor and monitoring of ongoing/ new legal cases against DRC.
- Supporting country director in keeping the registration status updated to incorporate changes in legal representative etc. by seeking timely support from legal advisors on the process.
- Advise and train HR and admin focal person in digitalization of HR and Admin tools and platforms.
- Coordination with finance unit to ensure payroll, taxes are captured accurately in the three countries.

**Learning and Development, Performance, and Well-being**

- Support managers & staff with performance management and review processes, including providing specialized trainings like People management skills.
- Act as an impartial mediator in disciplinary procedures and ensure that they follow DRC policies and meet all legal and labor regulations and requirements
- Implementation of Global, regional, and country level HR initiatives example (DRC Voices, minimum standards, staff wellbeing, diversity, and inclusion etc)
- Coordinate with senior managers to develop country wide training calendar.

**Compensation and Benefits**

- Take lead in salary review process in partnership with service provider, Finance team, Senior Management team at country and HQ and coordinate compensation review process and compensation adjustments.
- Analysis of benchmarking reports and the design of new salary grids; Support implementation of DRC’s new Compensation policy, including salary progression
- Prepare monthly payroll for Tunisia and review Algeria and Libya payroll to ensure compliance.
- Register employees in social security for all LE hosted by TUN legal entity.

**DRC Dynamics and Digitalization and reporting**

- Follow up the correct implementation of DRC Dynamics (HR Module) and the quality of the data entered in the system.
- Train HR focal person in TUN, Libya and Algeria and where required others in WANALA region.
- Monitoring accuracy and timely update of master data in dynamics for TUN, Libya and Algeria for the HR module
- Producing monthly HR reports for TUN, Libya and Algeria
- Ensure org chart for TUN, Libya and Algeria are up to date and produce when required by managers
- Develop/update HR templates digital/manual (recruitment tracker, onboarding and offboarding checklist and forms, recruitment request forms, exit clearance forms, contract request etc)
- Manage digital spaces like Share point (HR), MACH forms etc
- Provide training in Dynamics (HR Module) for HR focal person and relevant module like Employee self-service to new joiners
- Developing and maintaining full record of legal status/file of DRC’s registration in Tunisia.

**Partnerships:**

- Participate actively to the assessment of local partners capacities in terms of HR from the compliance and transparency perspective.
- Provide technical training to local partners in the fields covered by the scope of work of the HR coordinator Position.

**Code of Conduct**

- Will support country director in ensuring that required CoC structure is in place at country office.
- Coordinates with HQ and regional CoC focal person to seek technical inputs on the subject.
- Support country director in managing CoC structure in the country/operation.

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have at least 3 years’ working experience (officer and above) in Human Resources functions, preferably within an NGO.

Moreover, we also expect the following:

*Required*

- Demonstrated understanding and working knowledge/experience of Human Resources Management principles, concepts & processes
- Ability to interpret and transform local labor laws in DRC internal policies.
- Experience in developing Human Resources strategies and policies, and driving implementation
- Experience using an online system for recruitments and ERP system
- Payroll management and experience in salary benchmarking exercise
- Experience and understanding of local labour laws and managing legal services
- BA in Human Resources, Management, Administration or related subject is mandatory
- Fluency in French and Tunisian language is must
- Working knowledge of English is mandatory

*Desired*

- MA in a related subject is desired

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

Contract length: Open ended with 6 months probation period

Band: Non management G level 1

Designation of Duty Station: Tunis, Tunisia

Suggested Start date: 01 December 2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national employees; please refer to [our website](https://reliefweb.int/void(0)). For questions regarding the vacancy please contact [Us](https://reliefweb.int/void(0)).

**Application process**

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. **Applications sent by email will not be considered.**

title: Programme Coordinator - UKRAINE (M/F/X)
body:
**Working environment:**

The humanitarian situation in Ukraine remains critical amid ongoing international conflict. Since the escalation of the armed conflict on 24 February 2022, the destruction of vital civilian infrastructure continues to rise, leading to the destruction of homes across the country and cutting off access to critical services for millions of people. In 2025 in Ukraine, the UN estimates approximately 12.7 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance. Ukrainian refugee numbers abroad stand at about 6,9 million, while 3,7 million people are internally displaced (IDPs) within Ukraine.

The severe damage to critical infrastructure such as hospitals, schools, and water treatment plants has compromised access to clean water, sanitation, and essential healthcare services. Constant and long-lasting disruptions to the power grid have plunged entire regions into darkness, hindering communication and hampering daily life.

With the humanitarian situation in Ukraine being a challenge and may deteriorate further, the International Red Cross & Red Crescent Movement continues mobilising its emergency response mechanisms. Together, ICRC, IFRC, Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) and Partner National Societies (PNSs) are undertaking a coordinated response in contributing to URCS interventions as per One Plan 2023-27 and URCS Strategic Plan 2026-2030.

Reporting to the Head of Delegation, the Programme Coordinator will contribute to the development and implementation of the operational strategy of the Delegation, ensure the effective leadership of the country programme - including design, development, and implementation of the programmatic strategy, and contribute to the representation of the Delegation to partners, humanitarian coordination bodies and other relevant stakeholders.

**Missions:**

- **Strategy Development & Grants Management:** Leads on all aspects of programmatic design and actively develops the strategic & operational positioning as well as the development plan of the FRC UA Delegation, in support of the Head of Delegation. - **“National Society Development” Focus:** in the spirit of contributing to the partner’s sustainable development, participates actively in identifying the needs and priorities of URCS that are matching FRC’s international expertise and potential added-value; in order to develop FRC’s knowledge & understanding of URCS strategy and the NSD reference framework of IFRC and FRC.

- **Incumbent reporting line**: Reporting to Head of Delegation
- **Incumbent operational links:** HQ Desk Manager

**Qualifications and experience**

**Experiences :**

- At least 3 years’ experience in the same type of position in Coordination
- Previous experience in programme coordination positions
- Previous experience in supervising staff and supporting their professional and technical development.
- Experience and/or knowledge in communicating with various partners and donors
- Experience in developing new projects (concept note, proposal, budget, logframe, etc)
- Experience in donor reporting and contract management
- Experience working with local partners and partner-implemented projects / programmes
- Experience working with the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement
- Experience in donor reporting and financial contract management (previous experience with French donors is a strong asset: AFD, Expertise France, CDCS.
- Experience in the region and specifically in conflictual context is a strong asset
- Background in health or in health projects (including emergency medical services, nurse sciences, pre-hospital care, first aid, etc.) is a strong asset

**Education :**

- Studies in humanitarian or development project coordination or technical profile
- Mastery of the project cycle and project management tools
- Mastery of the humanitarian coordination system

**Skills**

**Mandatory job requirements**

- Organisational capacity
- Coordination capacity
- Strong writing and synthesis skills (for both proposals and reporting contributions)
- Effective capacity in grant management
- Effective capacity in MEAL procedures and processes
- Strong communication and diplomatic skills in multicultural work environments
- Teamwork skills (active listening, proactivity and consensus building)
- Experience in team management
- Initiative and ability to work efficiently and effectively without close supervision

**Valued skills**

- Proficiency in Office (Word, Excel, Powerpoint), networking (Google-Suite/Google Workspace)
- Expertise in identifying and implementing jointly capacity-improvement plans
- Experience facilitating trainings and accompanying staff to strengthen their expertise
- In-depth knowledge of the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement’s National Society Development approaches, especially through a Programme Coordination and Development lens

**Skills related to the specific environment of the mission:**

- Flexibility and quick adaptability
- Restraint, patience and diplomacy in institutional relations
- Ability to work within a coordination team and in functional link with the project and field teams
- Ability to work with a multicultural team
- Resilience to stress and high workload
- **International driving licence mandatory**

**Languages**

- English mandatory (oral and written);
- French or other language of the region would be an asset

**Conditions of employment:**

- Type of status: expatriate
- Type of contract: Fixed-term contract under French law
- Salary: According to the classification of the position on the CRf grid and the experience of the candidate
- Per diem: daily per diem which varies according to the country
- Leave: 10 to 15 days minimum every 6 months - Airfare paid at 100% by CRF for home travel
- Health coverage: CFE + Mutuelle MSH (covered 100%) - covered at 75% by the CRF
- MedEvac/repatriation insurance: YES
- Other insurances: Provident insurance (death and disability)

**SUMMARY**

- Location: Kyiv (with planned movements in Lviv, Kharkiv and possible other locations) - UKRAINE
- Duration: 12 months renewable
- Starting date: December 2026
- Mandatory driving licence

The French Red Cross reserves the right to close a recruitment before the closing date of the advertisement and the application deadline. Thank you for your understanding.

If we do not contact you within 3 weeks, please consider that we will not consider your application.

Female candidates are encouraged to apply.

title: Finance Manager Lebanon
body:
**What we are looking for**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has been supporting people affected by displacement in Lebanon for 20 years. As we embark on an important period of strategic and operational change, we are seeking an **experienced** **Finance Manager** to provide **strategic financial leadership**, **strengthen financial systems**, and ensure the effective and accountable use of resources to deliver humanitarian assistance.

We are looking for **a strategic, analytical, and solutions-oriented finance leader** who can navigate change, translate financial data into actionable insights, and balance strong financial controls with the operational flexibility required in a dynamic humanitarian context.

This is an exciting opportunity to shape NRC Lebanon’s financial direction, support organisational transformation, and strengthen collaboration with local partners and actors.

***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Lebanon, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***

**What you will do**

The Finance Manager is responsible for effective financial management, budgeting, reporting, compliance and internal controls across NRC Lebanon.

This role provides strategic financial leadership by delivering accurate, reliable, and timely financial information, enabling senior management to make informed decisions and ensure the efficient use of organisational resources.

The position holder will ensure that NRC Lebanon is well positioned to respond to current and future needs and shall demonstrate strong engagement and leadership in all major Finance actions, while ensuring capacity building for Finance team members and budget holders across the entire country.

Key responsibilities:

- **Provide strategic financial leadership** across NRC Lebanon, ensuring robust financial systems, policies, internal controls, and compliance with NRC, donor, and local regulatory requirements.
- **Lead budgeting, financial reporting, and analysis**, delivering timely, accurate insights to inform senior management decisions and support effective resource allocation.
- **Oversee accounting, cash flow, and liquidity management**, ensuring operational continuity, accurate financial records, and effective audit preparation and follow-up.
- **Manage financial risks and compliance**, strengthening accountability, implementing anti-corruption measures, and addressing audit findings and financial control gaps.
- **Advise and support budget holders and programme teams** throughout the project cycle, from proposal development and budgeting to expenditure monitoring and reporting.
- **Strengthen financial capacity and team performance** through effective leadership, staff development, and technical support to Finance colleagues and budget holders nationwide.
- **Advance NRC’s localisation agenda** by strengthening financial systems, tools, and capacity to support local partners and actors in delivering compliant, effective, and sustainable humanitarian responses.

**What you will bring**

- A bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, or a relevant field.
- **At least four years of finance experience**, including **three years in a managerial or equivalent role** **within a humanitarian or recovery context.**
- **Experience working with local partners** and **institutional humanitarian donors.**
- **Strong financial analysis**, **budgeting, reporting**, and risk management skills, with proficiency in MS Excel and accounting systems.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Experience **developing financial systems during organisational change** is highly desirable; **emergency finance leadership experience** and previous work in the Middle East are an advantage.

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDykXJd7GUEQZVDhD3vlo8xAUtc9vURiJeSfCAscQg3el0?e=oaBMOR) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Beirut, Lebanon
- Fixed term contract: 12 months national contract, renewable based on performance, funding and need for the position
- Travel: 10-20%
- Salary/benefits: Grade 9 on NRC's national grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- We invite applications from qualified candidates matching the profile. ***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Lebanon, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity

**Join NRC Lebanon and help shape the financial leadership, systems, and partnerships that will enable us to respond effectively to humanitarian needs and deliver greater impact.**

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

[Learn more about NRC Lebanon](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/lebanon)

title: Youth Program Supervisor
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**JOB OVERVIEW:**

The Youth Program Supervisor provides leadership and oversight for IRC's youth programming, including program operations, staff supervision, partnerships, compliance, resource development, and strategic planning. This role works collaboratively with staff, schools, families, and community partners to ensure high-quality services and positive outcomes for youth. The position reports to the Youth Education Manager.

 **MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES**

 **Program Design and Management:**

- Lead department and program planning in alignment with organizational mission and goals.
- Ensure high-quality services that empower youth and support their success in the community.
- Research, develop, and implement best practices that promote positive youth development and academic achievement for vulnerable youth.
- Establish and implement annual and long-term goals and objectives in collaboration with department leadership and staff.
- Ensure compliance with all program, donor, contractual, and IRC standards and requirements.
- Oversee accurate and timely financial, programmatic, and client recordkeeping, including use of ETO and ARRPODS systems.

**People Management**

- Supervise, coach, and support the professional growth and development of Youth Program staff.
- Lead training for staff and volunteers on education best practices, positive youth development, social-emotional asset development, and working with English Language Learners (ELLs).

**Resource Development and Partnership Development:**

- Contribute to grant and proposal development efforts to support and sustain programming.
- Develop, maintain, and strengthen relationships with school districts and strategic community partners.
- Represent IRC Youth Programs within the community and to current and prospective funders.
- Serve as a resource for information related to program activities.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

 **JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

- Bachelor's degree required; graduate degree in education, nonprofit management, public administration, social work, human services, or a related field preferred.
- Minimum three years of experience working with youth and two years of supervisory experience; experience with refugee and/or immigrant youth preferred.
- Demonstrated success in designing and implementing youth programs, leading staff, and building community partnerships.
- Strong communication, relationship-building, and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across diverse cultures, backgrounds, and perspectives, and uphold IRC values.
- Commitment to serving immigrant communities through trauma-informed and culturally responsive practices; bilingual abilities preferred.
- Valid driver's license, access to a personal insured vehicle, and ability to travel regularly throughout the service area.

 **Working Environment:**

A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities. Some evening and weekend hours will be required.  
  
**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $63,296.42/annual). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Job Overview**

The Early Childhood Education Specialist supports the implementation of early childhood and family-focused programming that promotes school readiness, family engagement, access to services, and positive outcomes for young children. This role works closely with families, childcare providers, educators, and community partners to strengthen early learning opportunities and support client success.

**Major Responsibilities**

**Program Implementation and Client Services**

- Implement early childhood education programming that promotes childcare access, school readiness, and family well-being.
- Assist families with accessing childcare assistance and enrolling in childcare services while identifying and addressing barriers to participation.
- Connect families with early learning opportunities, including Head Start, Early Head Start, preschool programs, and age-appropriate English Language Learning (ELL) services.
- Facilitate orientations and educational activities related to local resources, school systems, child welfare laws, parenting, and community integration.\\
- Support positive parent-child interactions and empower families through peer support, social groups, and parent education activities.

- Ensure compliance with grant requirements, reporting standards, and agency policies, including client confidentiality.

- Participate in meetings, trainings, and other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements**

title: Head of Advocacy and Evidencing
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**Location:** Ethiopia, India, Italy, Jordan, Kenya (as long as HelpAge International holds the registration in this country), Nepal, Pakistan, Spain, Tanzania, Thailand, Türkiye, United Kingdom and Zimbabwe

**Department:** Global Impact

**Reports to (Line Manager):** Director of Global Impact

**Responsible for (Line managing)**

- Humanitarian Advocacy Advisor
- Social Protection Advisor
- Health Advisor
- Rights Advisor

**Grade:** F

**Contract Type:** Open-ended contract

## **About HelpAge**

HelpAge International works with a diverse global network of around 200 organisations across 99 countries to promote the rights of older people to lead dignified, healthy and secure lives. Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience.

## **About the Job**

The Head of Advocacy & Evidencing provides strategic leadership and organisational accountability for HelpAge’s global advocacy, policy and research agendas, ensuring that external engagement is grounded in rigorous evidence, shaped by the lived experiences of older people, and aligned with organisational priorities.

## **Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities**

To deliver impact, the Head of Advocacy & Evidencing will:

- Lead the delivery and evolution of HelpAge’s global advocacy and research agenda, ensuring it reflects lived experience and drives progress on rights, inclusion, and equity for older people.
- Strengthen the capacities of network members and older people to lead and participate meaningfully in advocacy efforts, and ensure inclusive engagement in the design and implementation of influencing strategies.
- Cultivate strategic partnerships with policy, academic, and research institutions to co-produce high-quality, policy-relevant evidence and promote HelpAge’s thought leadership on rights, healthy ageing, humanitarian inclusion, and social protection.

## **Key Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership and Advocacy**

- Lead and be accountable for the development, implementation and results of HelpAge’s global advocacy and evidencing strategy, aligned with HelpAge’s impact areas and co-created with network members.
- Monitor and respond to global, regional and national policy trends,advising colleagues and network members on opportunities for engagement and influence.
- Champion inclusive, partner-led advocacy approaches that centre the voices and leadership of older people and civil society actors.
- Collaborate with the Fundraising and Strategic Partnerships Director and supporting members to align donor advocacy efforts with organisational priorities and global influencing strategies.
- Advise the Executive Leadership Group and the Board on HelpAge's advocacy positions and external positioning, and lead the preparation and quality of the related papers and briefings. Where appropriate, represent HelpAge's positions externally alongside senior leaders.
- Lead and coordinate HelpAge's influencing in priority global and regional policy and donor markets, including Europe, identifying opportunities to position ageing and the rights of older people within relevant policy, development and humanitarian agendas and, in collaboration with Fundraising, strengthen HelpAge's positioning with institutional donors and partners.
- Be accountable for achieving the agreed Advocacy & Evidencing income target. Working in partnership with the Fundraising & Strategic Partnerships team, play a lead technical and relationship role in shaping fundable propositions, contributing to pipeline development, and donor cultivation and stewardship for advocacy and research.
- Ensure that advocacy, research and evidence-generation activities comply with HelpAge’s ethical, safeguarding, data protection and relevant organisational standards, and hold team members accountable for compliance within their areas of responsibility.
- Represent HelpAge at senior level in key global and regional coalitions, alliances and policy forums, proactively building strategic relationships with governments, multilateral and donor institutions, policy actors and other influential stakeholders to advance HelpAge’s advocacy priorities and strengthen its external positioning.

**Evidence and Research**

- Lead and be accountable for HelpAge’s global research and evidence agenda, ensuring that it is coherent, ethical, inclusive and aligned with organisational advocacy and programme priorities.
- Provide strategic oversight of HelpAge’s global portfolio of evidence generation, policy analysis and advocacy initiatives across key impact areas, ensuring coherence, quality and alignment with organisational strategy and drawing on the network as a central source of evidence and insight.
- Foster partnerships with academic institutions, think tanks, and research bodies to co-produce and validate robust, policy-influencing evidence.
- Ensure that research outputs are accessible, actionable, and designed for strategic influence at global and national levels.

**Capacity Strengthening and Network Engagement**

- Lead on advocacy capacity strengthening of HelpAge network members and older people through mentoring, training, and tailored support.
- Promote knowledge exchange and peer learning across the global network, ensuring inclusive participation in advocacy platforms and decision-making spaces.
- Collaborate with regional colleagues to support the development and implementation of national and regional advocacy strategies led by network members.

**Team and Resource Management**

- Lead, manage, and coach a multidisciplinary team of advocacy advisers, ensuring high performance and alignment with organisational goals. These are hybrid roles, with approximately 50% of their time dedicated to global advocacy and the remaining 50% focused on technical support to network members and contribution to programme development.
- Manage advocacy and research budgets effectively, ensuring compliance with donor requirements and strategic resource allocation.

**Cross-Organisational Collaboration**

- Work closely with Programme Support, Network Development, MEAL, Fundraising, and Communications teams to embed evidence and influencing in all areas of work.
- Coordinate joint advocacy and research initiatives that connect policy engagement with programme delivery and impact measurement.

## **Skills and experience required**

*Essential*

- Proven strategic leadership in global advocacy, policy influencing, and research within the international development, humanitarian, or human rights sectors.
- Strong leadership, planning, and performance management skills, with a track record of delivering results through high-performing, diverse, and remote multidisciplinary teams.
- Deep understanding and practical application of rights-based, inclusive, and intersectional approaches—especially relating to age, gender, disability, and displacement.
- Demonstrated success in designing and implementing partner-led advocacy strategies that centre lived experience and community priorities.
- Experience influencing policy at national, regional and international levels through coalition-building and senior-level relationships with governments, multilateral bodies and donors.
- Strong analytical and research skills, with experience designing or overseeing ethical, participatory research and translating evidence into compelling policy and advocacy outputs.
- Demonstrated ability to build and sustain high-impact partnerships with academic institutions, think tanks and policy platforms.
- Track record of securing income for advocacy or research, including developing fundable propositions and engaging institutional donors with fundraising colleagues.
- Skilled in budget oversight and resource management, including accountability in donor-funded initiatives.
- Ability to monitor advocacy impact, policy trends, and funding landscapes, and to adapt strategies accordingly.
- Experience of strengthening the capacity of civil society, networks or grassroots movements, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, through mentoring, training and tailored support.
- Lived experience of the Global South or extensive professional experience working in Global South contexts.

*Desirable*

- Strong knowledge and networks in European/global institutional policy and donor environments
- Experience engaging with media to support advocacy.

**Education and Qualifications**

- Degree in international development, public policy, human rights, social sciences, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).
- A postgraduate qualification is an asset but not essential where practical experience is strong.

**Other Requirements**

- Willingness to travel internationally
- Ability to work across cultures, sectors, and geographies in inclusive and equitable ways.
- Excellent communication skills in English (spoken and written); additional languages used in the Global South (e.g., Spanish, French, Arabic) are highly desirable.
- Deep commitment to locally led development and the principles of Partner-Led Programming.
- We actively value and encourage candidates with lived experience of inequality, marginalisation, or systemic exclusion—especially related to age, gender, disability, displacement, or economic injustice.
- Familiarity with ageing, inclusion, and rights issues in Global South contexts is a key asset.

**Key Behavioural Competencies**

**Working Collaboratively with Others:** Work collaboratively, building mutual trust and respect, with external organisations and partners to achieve our strategic aims and objectives; being accountable for the work we do together.

**Adaptability and Flexibility:** Adapt to new directions or opportunities arising within the organisation and in our work area; being flexible in our role, constantly using the feedback to learn more and evolve further.

**Supporting and Facilitating Change:** Lead behavioural and cultural change through embracing a supportive, collaborative and highly inclusive environment where everybody feels supported, respected and engaged.

**Extend HelpAge’s Reach and Impact:** Extend HelpAge’s reach and impact by creating and identifying new business development opportunities and building relationships with new partners.

**Diversity and Inclusion:** Lead and promote a culture of including the voices of older people across our support, convening and thought leadership roles, in a way that is transformative, empowering and highly inclusive of those marginalised by gender, economic status, disability and other factors of discrimination.

**Leading Others (for managers):** Demonstrate strong leadership to own unit/department and manage people in a well and reputable manner. Create an atmosphere of trust and an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.

**Safeguarding**

HelpAge International is committed to safeguarding the communities with which we work, our partners, staff and any others who we come into contact with. The post holder will also be responsible for:

- Preventing harm and abuse from our people, operations and programmes to anyone that encounters our work.
- Reporting all safeguarding incidents you see, hear, hear about or suspect, using our internal reporting mechanism.
- Complying with all safeguarding framework policies and practices.
- Completing mandatory training courses relating to our safeguarding policy framework and complying with HR vetting procedures.

**SAFER RECRUITMENT**

All employments at HelpAge International will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include misconduct disclosure schemes and terrorism finance checks.

title: Field Volunteer – Women's Empowerment & Self-Defense in Athens
body:
## **About EmpowerVan**

[EmpowerVan](http://www.empowervan.org) is a non-profit organization dedicated to empowering women and girls on the move through self-defense and empowerment training. Our mission is to enable them to lead autonomous lives free from violence.

We currently operate programs in refugee camps and shelters for unaccompanied minors in Greece. There, we have a fully furnished van with martial arts equipment, that we drive to refugee camps, in order to teach self-defense to the people living there. We also go to shelters for unaccompanied minors and other spaces in Athens, to empower asylum seekers and refugees.

This year we have expanded our holistic approach to Kenya, bringing empowerment programs directly to women and girls in Kakuma Refugee Camp, where we certified refugees living in the camp as Empowerment Self-Defense Instructors, and men as Male Agents of Change, driving positive change in their community.

**Field Volunteer – Women's Empowerment & Self-Defense in Athens**

EmpowerVan is looking for a woman that is driven to advance gender justice, loves connecting with community members and has a passion for movement and sport. We are a small team and are looking for a volunteer to help us in Athens. You will be supporting us by going to classes in camps and shelters to support our instructors as you assist them, help with attendance, and you will also help us do reach-out to new community members, drive the van (is you have a license) and support us in daily tasks.

**What we’re looking for**

- **Teaching Skills**: Ability to teach sport, self-defense, or martial arts.
- **Gender Requirement**: Female applicants only (due to the nature of our work).
- **Personal Attributes**: Adaptable, well-organized, able to work independently, and at least 22 years old.
- **Experience**: Prior experience in sport and movement (hobby or work), experience working with displaced communities or minorities is preferred but not necessary.
- **Availability**: Able to be on the ground in **Athens for a minimum of 5 weeks**. Preferably afor at least 16 hours per week, up to full-time.
- People with a driver’s license highly preferred
- **Language skills:** Good spoken English is a must, as the team communicates in English.  
    Additional language skills are a huge plus, especially Persian, Arabic and French

## **Important Notes:**

- This is an **unpaid volunteer position**.
- Applicants must be self-sufficient and able to cover their own expenses during the volunteering period.
- We are not able to support with any visa process

If you’re ready to make a meaningful impact and join a dynamic team dedicated to creating a world free of gender-based violence, we’d love to hear from you!

title: Senior Economic Empowerment Manager
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:** The Sr. Economic Empowerment Manager coordinates the development, implementation, and completion of all grants, contracts and activities related to the Economic Empowerment department, including workforce development, small business development, financial capabilities, and career pathways programming. The Sr. Manager provides direct oversight of the Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) program and the One-Stop Operator program, supervising the RCA Program Manager and the One-Stop Operator Project Manager to ensure both programs are administered in compliance with donor, state, and federal requirements. The Sr. Manager also leads the ongoing development and long-term sustainability of workforce development and career pathways programming. Responsibilities include supervision of department staff to ensure program compliance across all Economic Empowerment programming.

**Responsibilities:** Include, but are not limited to:

**Oversight of Programs:**

- Effectively lead the development, implementation, compliance, and completion of Economic Empowerment grants and contracts.
- Responsible for the development of grant proposals and reports related to all areas of contracts and grants within the department.
- Supervise the provision of services through regular and systematic case file reviews, and quality assurance protocols including data QA to ensure compliance with donor requirements and provision of quality services.
- Lead all aspects of department program budget and manage expenses to ensure costs are maintained within allocated budgets.
- Provide oversight and strategic direction for the Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) program, supervising the RCA Program Manager to ensure timely, compliant delivery of cash assistance benefits to eligible refugee and new American clients in accordance with Arizona Department of Economic Security (ADES) and federal guidelines.
- Provide oversight and strategic direction for the One-Stop Operator program, supervising the One-Stop Operator Project Manager to ensure integration of workforce development services across system partners and compliance with federal and local workforce standards.
- Lead the development and long-term sustainability of workforce development and career pathways programming, including building new pathways, employer and community partnerships, and funding streams to support program growth.

**Staff Supervision and Other Responsibilities:**

- Directly supervise the RCA Program Manager and the One-Stop Operator Project Manager, in addition to other Economic Empowerment department staff, ensuring each program area is well-led, compliant, and resourced.
- Participate as an active member of the office leadership team and relevant internal and external groups.
- Lead the team members; formally evaluate team and individual performance to ensure objectives have been met.
- Recruit and train staff in all aspects of economic empowerment programs responsibilities.
- Represent IRC in public, professional and governmental forums. Build community partnerships and Lead local outreach to small businesses.
- Facilitate interdepartmental communication and information sharing for monthly newsletters, program reports, etc.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

- University degree (four year, B.A.) required; advanced degree in related field preferred.
- 5+ years of related program management experience including staff management, program development, and monitoring and evaluation.
- Previous fundraising and grant writing experience.
- Experience overseeing multiple concurrent programs and program managers preferred; familiarity with Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA)/ADES requirements and workforce system operations (e.g., WIOA, One-Stop/American Job Center models) is a strong plus.
- Demonstrated ability to promote an organizational culture that reflects IRC’s core values of service, accountability, integrity, and equality. Ability to lead through the true collaboration of individuals from many cultures with a great variety of skills and perspectives.
- Strong analytical and training skills; excellent written and oral communication skills.
- Highly organized self-starter with proven success managing multiple priorities, making critical decisions, and delivering results in a fast-paced environment with tight deadlines.
- Solid diplomacy, relationship building, and networking skills; ability to effectively manage internal and external relationships, including community stakeholders and donors.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written. Proficiency in a second language is desirable.
- Demonstrated proficiency in working with MS Office applications, with a strong command of Excel.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.
- Must possess or be eligible to receive an Arizona fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($69,939.00 - $92,500.00/annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Development of E-Learning Module Content — Tdh Migration and Displacement programme
body:
## **1. Background**

Terre des hommes (Tdh) is Switzerland's largest child rights organisation, active in over 30 countries. Its Migration and Displacement sector has developed two evidence-based Models of Action (MoA) to guide Tdh staff and partners working with migrant, displaced and at-risk children and youth:

**MoA 1 — Employability and access to employment for young migrants and refugees:** Employability and access to employment through (1) Skills and capabilities development, (2) Labour market linkage, and (3) Policy and system strengthening.

**MoA 2 — Education for children and youth on the move:** Structured around the 4As (Availability, Accessibility, Acceptability, Adaptability), leading to empowerment and socio-economic (re)integration.

Tdh wishes to make these frameworks accessible to its staff and implementing partners through the **development of related self-paced e-learning modules**. Tdh already runs a Migration and Displacement e-learning course for staff: the two new modules will be produced in the same format and uploaded to the existing platform by Tdh. This assignment covers content development only as platform integration is handled internally.

## **2. Objective and scope of work**

The consultant will develop content for two standalone e-learning modules, one for each MoA. The modules are intended for individual, self-paced learners. For each module, the consultant will submit a complete Word script that Tdh's technical team can upload to the existing CYM e-learning platform. The assignment does not include visual design, coding, platform configuration or upload work

**2.1 Consultant deliverables**

For each of the two modules, the consultant will deliver the following:

- Full content script (Word document): A complete, structured module script covering all learning content, activities and resources. The script must follow the format of the existing Tdh Migration and Development module series and be clear enough for Tdh's technical team to translate it into the online platform. It must include section text, activity instructions, external resource links with precise timecodes where relevant, correct answers for exercises, definitions and call-out boxes. It must be sufficiently clear and structured for the technical team to identify content blocks, activity types, correct answers, feedback text and any resources to be embedded or linked.
- Glossary: A list of 10-15 key terms with concise, learner-friendly definitions tailored to the thematic focus of the module.
- Learner summary sheet: A one-page printable reference sheet summarising the module's key concepts and takeaways, suitable for download alongside the module.
- Review and revision: The consultant will take part in an iterative review process, incorporate consolidated feedback from Tdh and submit revised versions until the module content is validated within the agreed workplan and timeline.

**2.2 Module format, components and minimum requirements**

Existing Migration and Development module scripts will be shared with the selected consultant as a formatting and style reference at the start of the assignment. Each module should follow the expected approach and minimum requirements below.

**Component**

1. Learner experience. **Expected approach:** Individual, self-paced learning. Content should be structured into short thematic sections that combine explanation, examples and activities. **Minimum requirement per module:** 45–60 minutes of learning time.
2. Narrative and voice. **Expected approach:** Write directly to the individual learner in the second person, using a clear and accessible register suitable for practitioners with varied educational backgrounds and operating contexts. **Minimum requirement per module** : Consistent second-person learner voice throughout the script.
3. Script length.**Expected approach :** Provide enough detail for direct platform integration, including all section text, activity instructions, answer keys and feedback text. **Minimum requirement per module** 2,500–4,000 words, including activity instructions and answers.
4. External resources. **Expected approach :** Curate publicly accessible, up-to-date and directly relevant resources, such as short videos, interactive data tools, websites, maps, reports or other practical materials. For any video used, provide precise start and end timecodes.**Minimum requirement per module** : Relevant external resources selected according to the learning objectives and availability of suitable materials. Each resource must include guided comprehension questions and correct answers where appropriate.
5. Interactive activities.**Expected approach :** Embed activities throughout the script and describe them clearly for platform build. Suitable formats include flip cards, matching or association exercises, multiple-choice questions, fill-in-the-blank questions and open reflection prompts. **Minimum requirement per module** : At least 2 interactive activities, plus at least 1 open reflection prompt. Correct answers and short feedback text must be provided where relevant.
6. Case studies.**Expected approach :** Use real-world or fictionalised case studies grounded in Tdh field contexts, including Asia, Africa and Europe/MENA where relevant. Cases should include named fictional or anonymised characters and guided analysis questions. **Minimum requirement per module** : At least 2 case studies, each with analysis questions and model answers.
7. Glossary and key concepts. **Expected approach :** Define core terms in concise, learner-friendly language and use call-out boxes to reinforce critical concepts, legal definitions, common misconceptions and section takeaways.**Minimum requirement per module** : At least 2 case studies, each with analysis questions and model answers.

## **3. Required profile**

## **Mandatory**

- Demonstrated experience writing e-learning content scripts or instructional materials for NGO or UN audiences
- Strong ability to translate programmatic frameworks into clear, engaging learning content for individual practitioners
- Capacity to identify and integrate high-quality external resources (videos, data tools, reports) into a structured learning narrative
- Substantive knowledge in at least one of the two thematic areas: youth employability, education in emergencies / migration
- Excellent written English; ability to write in a direct, accessible register suitable for diverse field staff

### **Advantageous**

- Familiarity with child rights frameworks and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
- Knowledge of all two thematic areas covered by the MoAs

title: Country Finance Manager Lebanon
body:
**Position**: Country Finance Manager Lebanon

**Location**: Beirut, Lebanon

**Reporting Relationship**: Country Representative (Line Management) and Regional Finance Manager (Functional Management)

**Family Duty Station**: NO

**Starting date**: ASAP

**Application deadline**: 07/11/2026

**Working Context**

WeWorld has been working in Lebanon since 2006 and is currently supporting vulnerable refugee, IDP and host community populations through WASH, Food Security and Livelihoods, Local Economic Development, Education and Social Cohesion in Bekaa, Baalbek-Hermel, Akkar, Saida and Beirut. Our interventions span immediate emergency response and recovery in view of building preparedness and longer-term resilience for populations affected by conflict and/or displacement. The operation is run by over 50 employees, divided in three offices (Beirut, Zahle and Saida). We work closely with local partners, including NGOs and institutional actors at different levels, and are part of large consortia with other actors.

**Purpose of the Role**

The **Country Finance Manager** is responsible for all the administrative and accounting processes, including financial reporting, budget planning, development and monitoring. They manage staff within the Finance Department in country.

**MAIN FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES**

**General Administration**

- Track and manage deliverables and timelines related to grants, contracts, vendors, and partners
- Monitor grant administration to ensure compliance with reporting and expenditure requirements
- Supervise compliance of administrative documents and their proper filing
- Ensure the smooth flow of administrative information and data to the HQ
- Supervise flow of administrative information from project partners and the compliance with MoU
- Ensure smooth and punctual communications and reporting with local banks

**Accounting**

- Supervise and approve regular accounting, including monthly reconciliations, monthly and yearly closing of accounts, monthly journal entries
- Supervise cash and bank balance checking process when closing the monthly accounts

**Financial Reporting**

- Responsible for the preparation of financial reports, in coordination with Regional Finance Manager, and administrative team
- Ensure the compliance of financial reports with donors’ and internal rules and procedures

**Budget & Planning**

- Prepare and regularly monitor/updateWeWorld’s core budget for the Lebanon operation and provide an analysis to the Country Representativefocusing on gaps and risks
- Collaborate with the Country Representative, Head of Programmes and Project Managers to develop project budgets with quality, on time, in line with the operation’s core budget and according to donors’ regulations;
- Review administrative/financial terms of grant contracts before signature (payment & financial reporting schedule, etc.)
- Collaborate with the Head of Programmes, Project Managers and Procurement & Logistics Managers to regularly monitor actual and forecasted expenses against budget to avoid under and overspending on the projects in compliance withdonor flexibility rules
- Monitor financial flows of ongoing projects
- Anticipate financial risks, present budget updates and mitigation plans and report them to the Country Representative;
- Participate with the Country Management Team in reflecting on the evolution of the mission, and the programming of new projects and/or reorientation

**Audit Process**

- Collaborate to the management of financial audit performed on the projects
- Supervise yearly financial audit on general accounting for local authorities
- Prepare information and is directly responsible for any assessment/audit performed by donor on WeWorld administrative procedure

**Procedure**

- Design and implement administrative routines, procedures, and systems to increase efficiencies within the finance department, in particular relating to better structuring Budget Follow Ups, Forecasts, Payment Follow Ups and optimizing staff roles and responsibilities within the team
- Update the Local Operational Manual based on WeWorld procedures to implement organizational policies related to the Finance Department

**Operational**

- At Country level, liaise with the Human Resources and Procurement and Logistic departments for a fluid and collaborative collaboration
- Follow-up payments from donors and financial project close-out

**Human Resources**

- Participate in analyzing staffing needs & costs, compensation & benefits
- Supervise administrative and finance local personnel to complete routine tasks
- Capacity building of local finance staff and partner organizations in areas such as financial management, administration, good governance and management of accountability and transparency
- Support the Country Representative and the HR Manager to monitor and revise salary scale, if necessary

**Representation**

- Participate in inter-admin meetings with other INGOs and NGOs
- Ensure official representation for the administrative management of the Mission to the competent authorities

The duties and responsibilities set forth above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to perform additional duties requested by the Line Manager. Proper handover must be ensured before the end of the assignment.

**WHAT WE OFFER**

title: Psychiatrist or Clinical Psychologist - West Africa
body:
**Position summary:**

Shelter For Life International (SFL) is anticipating a project in West Africa with a focus on managing the flow of migrants into the region. Included in the project’s objectives will be structured movement and resettlement of migrants within and outside Guinea-Bissau, while providing basic food, shelter and other humanitarian assistance.

SFL is seeking a clinical psychologist to provide mental health and social support to migrants in West Africa. The clinical psychologist will be responsible for designing and implementing a psychological and psychosocial support program for migrants who are navigating displacement and resettlement. This role involves providing direct clinical care, occasional crisis intervention, and building the capacity of local staff to ensure culturally appropriate mental health services during the resettlement process. The position will be based in Bissau, Guinea-Bissau.

**Areas of Responsibility:**

- Conduct psychological assessments and provide professional mental health support to newly arrived and transitioning migrants, with referral to in-country medical professionals if needed.
- Develop and implement support protocols for individuals experiencing stress or trauma.
- Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, including medical staff as needed, to ensure a holistic approach to migrant well-being and basic needs.
- Conduct psychoeducational workshops to help migrants cope with acculturative stress, build resilience, and prepare for resettlement in new host countries.
- Maintain strictly confidential clinical records and monitor mental health trends within the migrant population to adapt programs and inform SFL management.

**Education and Experience Requirements:**

- Medical doctor degree (M.D., D.O., or M.B.B.S.) with Psychiatry residency, Master’s degree or Doctorate (Ph.D. or Psy.D.) in Clinical Psychology from an accredited institution.
- Valid professional license to practice clinical psychology in your home jurisdiction.
- Minimum of 3 to 5 years of post-graduate clinical experience, specifically focusing on trauma, displacement, or working with refugee/migrant populations.
- Must be fluent in English (written and spoken), with a working knowledge of Spanish. Additional language skills relevant to the demographic context (e.g., French, Portuguese) are a plus.
- Proven experience working in humanitarian emergencies, international development, or low-resource, post-conflict settings.
- Experience in cross-cultural counseling and effectively conducting clinical sessions with the assistance of language interpreters.

**Personal Skills and Abilities:**

- Exceptional cross-cultural communication skills and sensitivity to the diverse religious, cultural, and social backgrounds of multi-national migrants.
- Strong adaptability and psychological resilience, with the capacity to thrive in a dynamic and challenging physical environment with limited local amenities.
- High emotional intelligence and the ability to maintain strong professional boundaries to prevent burnout in a high-stress environment.
- Collaborative leadership style with the ability for capacity-building and empowering local staff for assistance.
- Sound judgment, strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to make rapid clinical decisions independently in the event of crises.
- Commitment to the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence, as well as the core mission of Shelter For Life International.

SFL is interested in applicants whose professional ethics, values, and determination to achieve impact are evident and aligned with organizational priorities.

Additional Notes:

- A minimum of 12 months' commitment to live and work in Guinea-Bissau is required.
- Applicants must be comfortable with travel within the project area.
- Competitive pay and benefits, including paid time off, ACA-compliant health insurance, and housing allowance.

Job description in PDF here: [https://shorturl.at/gYIwz](https://shorturl.at/gYIwz)

**About us:**

Shelter For Life International (SFL) is an international faith-based relief and development organization with over 30 years’ experience providing sustainable development and humanitarian assistance to post-conflict countries worldwide. We are currently operational in Afghanistan, The Gambia, and Ukraine, with headquarters located in Minnetonka, MN, USA. Our team provides support and assistance in the following areas:

1. Population Movement and Settlement
2. Public Infrastructure Reconstruction
3. Economic and Social Development

Our mission is to demonstrate God’s love by enabling people affected by conflict and disaster to restore their lives and rebuild their communities. To learn more about us, please visit [www.shelter.org](http://www.shelter.org/)
